precepts.text: Those "in league" are the peoples in agreement or alliance with Ethiopia, who fall together with Egypt by the sword.
precepts.point: Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, all the mingled people, and the men of the land that is in league shall fall with them by the sword; those that uphold Egypt shall fall and the pride of her power come down.
precepts.why:
“Ethiopia, and Libya, and Lydia, and all the mingled people, and Chub, and the men of the land that is in league, shall fall with them by the sword.” Those “in league” are the peoples in agreement or alliance with Ethiopia. They are joined to Egypt and Ethiopia, so they fall together with them by the sword.

This is the day of the Lord, “a cloudy day; it shall be the time of the heathen.” The sword comes upon Egypt and “great pain shall be in Ethiopia”, and everyone who upholds Egypt falls: “the pride of her power shall come down”. Being in league with her does not save you; it puts you in the same fall, desolate in the midst of the countries that are desolate.

moments.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: Ezekiel is to prophesy, Woe worth the day, for the day of the Lord is near, a cloudy day, the time of the heathen; the sword shall come upon Egypt and great pain in Ethiopia when the slain fall.
Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, all the mingled people, and the men of the land that is in league shall fall with them by the sword; those that uphold Egypt shall fall and the pride of her power come down.

The Most High will make the multitude of Egypt to cease by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and the terrible of the nations, who draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain, drying the rivers and selling the land into the hand of the wicked.

He will destroy the idols, cause the images to cease out of Noph, set fire in Egypt, pour His fury upon Sin, cut off the multitude of No, and send the cities of Egypt into captivity, so they shall know that He is the Lord.
In the eleventh year the word came that the Most High has broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and it shall not be bound up to be healed or made strong to hold the sword.
He will break both Pharaoh's arms, strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put His sword in his hand, scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and they shall know that He is the Lord.

What we’re reading here is future prophecy. “Even the day of the Lord is near”: that’s the key. It is the day of the Lord, not something long finished. “It shall be the time of the heathen”: the time of the heathen meaning their destruction.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “And the sword shall come upon Egypt”: destruction shall come on Egypt, and right now it’s Arabs there in Egypt. On the map you got Egypt, which includes Sudan, and then you got Ethiopia: “great pain shall be in Ethiopia, when the slain shall fall in Egypt”.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “Ethiopia, and Libya, and Lydia, and all the mingled people, and Chub”. Y’all see Libya right next to Egypt: Libya going to get it, Egypt going to get it. Lydia, that’s Turkey. Chub is Chad; write that down: Chub is Chad, Chad is Chub. “And the men of the land that is in league, shall fall with them by the sword”: they all going to get it.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “They also that uphold Egypt shall fall”: anybody that upholds Egypt shall fall. “From the tower of Syene shall they fall in it by the sword”: the tower of Syene is what they call Aswan today.

The encyclopedia says Syene was always the last town of Egypt on the south, though at one time it was included in the name Nubia, and Nubia is modern day Sudan. Look up Nubia: it runs from Aswan in southern Egypt down to the confluence of the Blue and White Niles in Khartoum in central Sudan. That lets you know it’s one place; they separated it.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “When all her helpers shall be destroyed”: anybody that helps Egypt in this coming world’s war is going to be destroyed. The Arabs took over Libya, they took over Egypt, so that’s the Arabs there; but then you got the Hamites, a lot of them in Chad, the Sudan area and Ethiopia. We know our people are scattered there too, but we’re not talking about our people here; we’re talking about the Hamites.

Although there’s Hamites there, the scholars know there’s Israelites in Sudan. Hebrewisms of West Africa by Joseph J. Williams, copyright 1930, tells of a manuscript that refers to a Jewish tribe in what is now the English Sudan (they call it English Sudan because Britain had taken it over) as El Yahood. That’s what the Arabs called us: Yahood, meaning Judah. It even ties the word to Yaho, the name of the Supreme Being that we call Yahawah, and says these Jews might be descendants of the old colonists of the Nile. The scholars know. They know, now we know.

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: “In that day shall messengers go forth from me in ships to make the careless Ethiopians afraid, and great pain shall come upon them, as in the day of Egypt: for, lo, it cometh.”

note.label: From Egypt to Rome | From Sudan to Babylon

points: Then he jumps back to Nebuchadnezzar, and Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon. Notice verse two talks about the day of the Lord, then verse ten jumps back to Nebuchadnezzar.
